name: Hesiodic Theogony cosmogony

surviving_manuscript_date.note: M. L. West notes that the earliest complete manuscripts of the Theogony date only from the end of the thirteenth century; this range stores the century rather than inventing an exact manuscript year.

estimated_composition.method: Modern philological datings cluster around the late eighth to mid-seventh century BCE: Janko c. 700–665 and West c. 680–660.

tradition_internal_claim.note: The poem narrates the coming-to-be and generations of gods in primordial time rather than assigning a historical date.

estimated_oral_origin.method: The poem stands within an older Greek poetic/oral environment, but no absolute date for its precursors is asserted here.

dating.dating_summary: Modern scholarship generally places the Theogony around the late eighth to mid-seventh century BCE; the earliest complete surviving manuscripts are much later, at the end of the thirteenth century CE.

notes: The narrative begins with Chaos, Gaia, Tartarus, and Eros and proceeds through divine generations and succession conflicts.
